summary: Intermittent timeouts for EU customers caused by stale edge-route TTL and cross-region fallback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NexusAI reports intermittent 5xx timeouts and severe latency spikes for inference requests originating in eu-central. Requests occasionally take >8s or fail with 504 Gateway Timeout. The pattern began ~2026-03-10 03:00 UTC and has recurred with short windows of normal traffic.

Impact:
- Affects production traffic for a dedicated NexusAI deployment (eu-central).
- Observed increase in 504/502 rates and tail latency for token generation endpoints.
- Business impact: degraded user experience and failed inference requests for key customers.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted dedicated nodes for NexusAI in eu-central.
- Edge proxy pool (regionally distributed) routes to serving runtime clusters (eu-central primary, us-east fallback).
- Routing TTL for edge-route affinity set to 120s (recent config change on 2026-03-08).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send stream generation requests from an eu-central client with model redwood-ggml-13b pinned to the dedicated deployment.
2) Observe occasional long polling times (>8s) and 504/502 responses.
3) Repeat during peak window (03:00-05:00 UTC local monitoring showed increased frequency).
4) Verify edge-proxy logs for request hash and backend target resolution.

Notes: issue is intermittent; reproduction depends on short window where edge route affinity TTL produces stale cross-region mapping.
observed_behavior:
- 504 Gateway Timeout returned by edge-proxy when backend route points to us-east serving cluster under temporary connectivity degradation.
- Traces show initial connection attempts to eu-central then a redirect/fallback to us-east after edge-route TTL expiration.
- Increased TCP retransmits and higher NACKs on peered links seen around same timestamps.
expected_behavior:
- Requests from eu-central should consistently route to eu-central serving runtime (primary), and only fallback to us-east when primary is unhealthy, with graceful failover and preserved client-side timeouts.
- No stale route affinity should persist past configured TTL and route selection should not force cross-region results under transient peering flaps.
logs_and_traces:
Selected traces (timestamps UTC):
- 2026-03-10T03:12:07Z trace-id=trc_9a7: edge-proxy resolved backend=us-east-rt-04 after TTL expiry, backend responded 504 after 8.2s.
- 2026-03-10T03:12:09Z netlogs: BGP flap event reported by cloud-provider peering (urn:peer/eu-to-us) lasting ~18s.
- 2026-03-10T03:12:10Z serving-runtime logs (us-east): high connection queue, slow KV cache warmup.
Links: Kibana logs: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/kibana#/discover/edge-proxy?q=trace-id:trc_9a7
P99 traces: https://apm.redwood.ai/traces?service=edge-proxy&time=2026-03-10T03:00:00Z
investigation_notes:
1) Timeline: peering BGP event coincides with first spike window. Edge-route affinity TTL configuration change on 2026-03-08 (reduced from 300s to 120s) likely increased frequency of route re-resolution.
2) Hypothesis: Short TTL combined with transient peering degradation causes edge-proxies to resolve backend as unreachable in eu-central and immediately route to us-east fallback. The fallback path encounters rate limits/backpressure and results in timeouts.
3) Evidence: Edge-proxy metrics show 'route-resolve' spike and 'backend-fallback' counts matching BGP flap timestamps. Serving runtime in eu-central shows brief drop in ready workers (likely connection churn).
4) Customer-specific config: NexusAI uses strict model pinning and no multi-region sticky caching; their dedicated routing policy had been recently adjusted to allow fallback to us-east for capacity reasons.
5) Related PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/842 changed TTL logic; needs review for corner-case handling.
mitigation_workaround:
1) Temporarily increase edge-route affinity TTL to 600s for NexusAI dedicated pool to reduce re-resolution churn (applied at 2026-03-10T04:00Z).
2) Apply conservative fallback throttle to prevent immediate cross-region spill during peering events (rate-limit fallback to 10r/s).
3) Notify NexusAI of changes and ask them to extend client-side timeout to 15s during investigation if acceptable.
4) Monitor p99 latency and 5xx rate for 6h post-mitigation.
resolution_notes:
Root cause: combination of aggressive edge-route TTL reduction and transient provider peering degradation led to frequent backend re-resolution and cross-region fallback into overloaded us-east backends, producing timeouts.
Fixes applied:
- Reverted TTL change for dedicated pools to 600s (config rollback) on 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC.
- Edge-proxy PR updated to add a 'grace window' that suppresses fallback for 30s after a route resolve if BGP/peering instability is detected (merged and deployed to staging PR/842, production rollout scheduled).
- Added monitoring alert (alert id A-EDGE-ROUTE-01) to detect high rate of backend-fallback events.
Follow-up: longer-term review of fallback throttling and regional capacity margins; ops ticket INT-3392 created to track autoscale policy adjustments for dedicated customers.
